newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1997 world, U.S. wheat crop estimates.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1997 world, U.S. wheat crop estimates.

text.p: The International Grains Council raised its estimate for 1997 world wheat production to 585 million tonnes on Thursday from its 579 million estimate a month ago and against 1996 output of 582 million tonnes.

In its monthly Grains Market Report the IGC said much of the growth came from better expectations from the US, where the estimate was raised to 66 million tonnes from the previous 62.6 million, and with 62.1 million estimated for 1996.
Yields are much better than earlier expected, the IGC said. Dry weather has allowed harvesting to be completed in Illinois, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas.

Russia and Ukraine both did well, with the Russian estimate up to 36.5 million tonnes compared with the previous 34 million and a 1996 crop of 34.9 million. Russian production has been boosted by favourable weather, the IGC said.
It lifted its estimate for Ukraine's wheat crop to 19 million tonnes from the previous 17 million (13.4 million in 1996). Yields in Ukraine were reported to be the best in three years, it said.

There was also more optimism about some big Asian producers. The IGC revised China's 1997 wheat crop up to 113.5 million tonnes compared with the previous 112 million (109 million in 1996) after reports of higher yields in key provinces Henan and Shandong. India's crop was raised to 66 million tonnes from a previous 65 million (62.6 million in 1996) and Pakistan's to 17 million from 15.8 million previously and 16.9 million tonnes output in 1996. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
